title: Cut & harvest
detail: Ripe cane cut; cane processed quickly to prevent sugar content declining; harvest 5–6 months after planting on fertile plantations; simultaneous cutting + transport + crushing + boiling in harvest season.

title: Transport to crusher
detail: Cane carried to crushing sites; rails/conveyors later; proximity to rivers & ports lowers cost; enslaved people cart cane.

title: Crushing
detail: Fed through rollers into crushing device; juice extracted; dangerous work; arms drawn into rollers; presses hand→3-cylinder→wind/water→steam; two-roller horizontal mill.

title: Boiling & concentration
detail: Juice boiled in series of large vats/cauldrons; concentrated to thick syrup; 'curing'; large fuel requirement; timber or bagasse; copper pans + coal in European refineries; vacuum pans.

title: Cool in inverted cones
detail: Cooled in inverted earthenware cones; separation into sugar loaves and molasses.

title: Molasses separated
detail: Crystallisation/refining; molasses extracted; molasses → rum (17th c. onward); later centrifuge.

title: Curing → loaf
detail: Poured into sizeable clay pots/moulds; hardened cone-shaped sugar loaves.

title: White sugar
detail: Clay + water mixture on broad side of cone; molasses drips out; drained; loaves dried on racks; trimmed; wrapped in paper.

title: Final refining (Europe)
detail: Colonies produce brown loaf/muscovado; final whitening in British/Dutch towns; re-export; tax policy; 'not even a nail'; modern plants 'bleach' brown sugar.
